scope: Prelaunch-owned process-tree closure for new native evaluations, including native legacy-report and JSON-observation adapters. Not a domain-specific research optimization.

new_test_classification.note: Three public paths prove one natural-exit ownership gap. The baseline is the preceding implementation commit, not an assertion about a released product. Missing APIs, setup/fixture failures and repeated runs are not counted as historical bugs.
new_test_classification.mechanisms: 10 supervisor API cases + 13 binding validation cases + 3 initially passing native adapter cases + 3 real shutdown/HOLD cases.
new_test_classification.drafts: 3 post-spawn/fork handoff faults + 1 missing-protocol started admission + 2 READY-to-GO revalidation faults.

implemented: Commit protocol-tagged LAUNCHING intent before supervisor creation; READY carries actual worker PID/start ticks, separate supervisor identity, full AttemptRef/scope and digests.

Durably bind native RUNNING/compute start before GO; recheck controller runtime and prepared B2 inputs before allowing execution. Known blocked initialization failures are stopped; uncertain handoffs HOLD.
Dedicated Linux subreaper owns orphan descendants including detached double-fork workers. Natural leader exit alone does not publish and does not kill useful descendants.

Integer completion requires matching TREE_CLOSED, actual worker status, ECHILD with __WALL, and normal supervisor exit. STOP targets only direct/adopted owned children through pidfds; no native-evaluation PGID discovery fallback.

Both direct native publishers and shutdown verify full stored binding/closure before effects and again in the short transaction. Persist full closure in terminal/effect plan; stopped worker zero cannot produce successful evaluation observations.
Historical native rows without protocol cannot be enrolled from bare PID. Genuine no-catalog legacy Popen remains unsupervised; supported Linux is now required for new native evaluation.
